bull_bear.body:
- Port-linked manufacturing at Gandhidham, Haldia, Krishnapatnam and Mangalore located near key ports including Kandla, strengthening sourcing efficiency, reducing transportation costs and enhancing export competitiveness
- Fully integrated value chain from seed procurement and crushing through refining, packaging and distribution, enabling flexible product mix planning and swift response to demand shifts
- Scale in refining with 2 Million MTPA capacity and capacity utilisation averaging around 83% across refining and seed-crushing units
- Distribution reach of 575+ distributors, a hub-and-spoke logistics model and presence across 28 states and 33 countries
- Institutional credibility with large food manufacturers being extended into a unified B2B and B2C trust platform, with established consumer brands Vitalife and Mahek
- Comprehensive internationally recognised food safety and quality certifications operating under a single unified quality governance framework across all products
- Over 40 years of promoter expertise in the edible oil industry, with the Chairman & Managing Director a first-generation entrepreneur with over four decades in the sector
- Unified digital core on SAP S/4HANA spanning procurement, manufacturing, inventory, finance, sales and distribution, with DCS-based real-time process monitoring and batch-level traceability
- Captive renewable power from wind and solar utilised across all four manufacturing locations, plus use of castor meal as boiler fuel in place of coal, lowering production costs
- Product-mix breadth spanning consumer edible oils, industrial castor derivatives, institutional supply, biodiesel and global exports, diversifying the demand base within the oils value chain
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Single-activity concentration in edible and non-edible oils — The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from one main activity, Edible Oils, Food, FMCG and Industry Essentials, with Edible Oils & Byproducts at 90.88% and Non Edible Oils & Byproducts at 9.12% of turnover, so there is no earnings diversification outside the oils value chain.
- Commodity price volatility in an inherently thin-margin business — The Corporate Overview describes the commodity market the Company was built in as one that runs on volume, volatility and thin margins, where efficiency, integrated sourcing and logistics reach separate survival from leadership, so small swings in oilseed and edible oil prices bear directly on profitability.
- Exposure to global supply, freight and geopolitical disruption through imports and exports — The Company sells across 28 states and 33 countries with exports at 8.11% of turnover, and the forward-looking disclaimer explicitly qualifies the report by the risk factors in the MD&A, flagging that assumptions and predictions may not prove accurate.
- High workforce attrition, particularly among permanent workers — BRSR turnover rates rose year on year: permanent employees to 26.62% in FY26 from 22.32% in FY25 and permanent workers to 39.78% from 29.02%, a structural retention and operating-continuity concern in plant operations.
- Customer concentration in B2B institutional sales — The BRSR states the Company's historical strength lies in B2B sales, naming PARLE Biscuits, Haldiram Snacks, Pratap Snacks, Gopal Snacks, ITC, Britannia and Balaji Wafers among its clientele, so a small set of large food manufacturers carries meaningful volume.
- Geographic concentration of manufacturing in a small number of national plants — BRSR Section A records 4 plants and 1 office, all national with no international sites, so operational disruption at any single facility is not readily absorbed elsewhere.
- Ongoing tax and customs litigation — The notes disclose appeals pending with GST authorities, an income-tax matter under section 148 before the Gujarat High Court and a customs matter before CESTAT Ahmedabad; management assesses these as only possible and expects no material financial impact, but they remain open proceedings.
- Governance concentration in a promoter family with related-party breadth — The Board comprises 8 directors with 4 executive directors drawn from the promoter family, women are 12.50% of the Board, and the related-party roster lists numerous entities under KMP significant influence or control, raising oversight and related-party-transaction scrutiny.

business.body: The Company is engaged in the production, distribution and export of edible oils, non-edible oils and their derivatives and feed meals in India, describing itself as one of the leading and fastest growing companies in the segment. Its portfolio spans edible oils, vanaspati, bakery fats, castor oil and derivatives, specialty fats, biodiesel and glycerin, supported by an integrated value chain running from seed procurement and crushing through refining, packaging and distribution. It serves household consumers, restaurants, food service providers, food manufacturers, retailers and wholesalers domestically and worldwide, with a historical strength in B2B institutional supply that it is now extending into branded consumer sales.

outlook.body:
- Scale the branded and value-added portfolio to capture India's edible oil demand tailwinds, with the MD&A stating Gokul Agro is well-positioned to capture these tailwinds as it scales its branded and value-added portfolio
- Compete through an integrated model rather than scale alone, leveraging integrated sourcing, refining, port-linked infrastructure and a distribution-led model as the MD&A describes as strategically valuable given India's structural import dependence
- Build a self-reinforcing engine of adjacent businesses, with the Corporate Overview stating every investment over the past several years has been designed to reinforce the one before it and that growth beyond the commodity ceiling demands integration
- Move up the value chain into higher-margin premium, cold-pressed, fortified and speciality oil segments as health-led premiumisation reshapes product portfolios
- Extend the castor derivatives franchise into bio-based chemicals, cosmetics, lubricants and pharmaceutical excipient applications where India holds over 85% of global castor seed production
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Gokul Agro operates an integrated, port-linked manufacturing footprint across Gandhidham, Krishnapatnam, Haldia and Mangalore, and the MD&A states the Company now has 2 Million MTPA of oil refining capacity, 1 Million MTPA of seed-crushing capacity and 2.5 lacs MTPA of speciality products and biodiesel capacity. Supply-chain infrastructure supporting this platform comprises 37,000 MT of silos capacity, 2,10,000 MT of liquid storage capacity and 50,000 MT of seed and DOC warehousing capacity. During FY26 the Company invested Rs 150 cr in capital expenditure primarily for the Biodiesel plant and the Captive Solar Power project in Gujarat, reinforcing its manufacturing and operating capabilities, with net debt of Rs 297 cr described as largely reflecting investments in strategic expansion and capital expenditure. On the project side, the Directors Report records that the Company commenced operations of a biodiesel plant with a capacity of 300 MTPD during FY 2025-26, with output primarily exported to European countries where demand for renewable fuels is strong; in the prior year FY 2024-25 the Company initiated palm plantation activities in Ananthapur District, Andhra Pradesh covering 100.73 hectares of land under the National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO), described as a significant step towards backward integration and sustainable raw material sourcing. Within existing plants, a debottlenecking step is described in the energy-conservation disclosure: an 800 TPD separator was installed in the refinery neutralisation section in place of two 400 TPD separators, increasing production capacity from 1200 TPD to 2000 TPD while reducing power consumption. Capacity utilisation is stated as averaging around 83% across refining and seed-crushing units, and captive renewable generation is in place, with power generated from wind and solar utilised in the manufacturing units and offices across all 4 locations.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's structural edible oil supply-demand gap: domestic production meets only about 40% of annual demand, requiring imports of nearly 16 million tonnes per year costing USD 18-19.5 billion, which management frames as the strategic case for domestic processing capacity
- Indian macro support: real GDP is projected to grow 6.8-7.2% in FY27, underpinned by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment and broadening private-sector participation, with stable inflation and rising incomes sustaining purchasing power
- Durable structural tailwinds for agri-processing, FMCG and edible oil businesses from rising rural consumption, expanding food-processing activity and growing preference for branded and packaged products
- India's edible oil market at 25.33 million tonnes in 2025 projected to reach 28.34 million tonnes by 2034 at a 1.26% CAGR, with value growth expected to outpace volumes as premiumisation accelerates
- Health-led premiumisation shifting demand toward fortified, high-oleic and speciality oils, reshaping product portfolios and opening higher-margin segments
- The fuel-versus-food dynamic: rising use of edible oils for biodiesel and aviation fuel is tightening supply, linking edible oil prices directly to energy markets and amplifying volatility
- Global edible oils market growth from USD 253.67 billion in 2025 to USD 362.80 billion by 2034 at a 4.06% CAGR, with Asia-Pacific holding the largest regional share at 53%
- Global castor oil demand growth from 977.72 KMT in 2025 to 1,391.12 KMT by 2035 at a 3.59% CAGR, driven by bio-based chemicals, electric vehicles, cosmetics and sustainable fuels
- Government policy support including the National Mission on Edible Oils, organised retail and e-commerce expansion, enabling capture of higher-value segments and reduced import exposure
- Watchpoints management names against this: weather disruptions and global volatility in vegetable oil prices, with commodity prices expected to remain volatile
- Sustainability becoming a structural requirement, with stricter regulations and consumer scrutiny pushing producers toward certified, traceable and environmentally responsible supply chains

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- India's structural edible oil supply-demand gap: domestic production meets only about 40% of annual demand, requiring imports of nearly 16 million tonnes per year costing USD 18-19.5 billion, which management frames as the strategic case for domestic processing capacity
- Indian macro support: real GDP is projected to grow 6.8-7.2% in FY27, underpinned by domestic consumption, infrastructure investment and broadening private-sector participation, with stable inflation and rising incomes sustaining purchasing power
- Durable structural tailwinds for agri-processing, FMCG and edible oil businesses from rising rural consumption, expanding food-processing activity and growing preference for branded and packaged products
- India's edible oil market at 25.33 million tonnes in 2025 projected to reach 28.34 million tonnes by 2034 at a 1.26% CAGR, with value growth expected to outpace volumes as premiumisation accelerates
- Health-led premiumisation shifting demand toward fortified, high-oleic and speciality oils, reshaping product portfolios and opening higher-margin segments
- The fuel-versus-food dynamic: rising use of edible oils for biodiesel and aviation fuel is tightening supply, linking edible oil prices directly to energy markets and amplifying volatility
- Global edible oils market growth from USD 253.67 billion in 2025 to USD 362.80 billion by 2034 at a 4.06% CAGR, with Asia-Pacific holding the largest regional share at 53%
- Global castor oil demand growth from 977.72 KMT in 2025 to 1,391.12 KMT by 2035 at a 3.59% CAGR, driven by bio-based chemicals, electric vehicles, cosmetics and sustainable fuels
- Government policy support including the National Mission on Edible Oils, organised retail and e-commerce expansion, enabling capture of higher-value segments and reduced import exposure
- Watchpoints management names against this: weather disruptions and global volatility in vegetable oil prices, with commodity prices expected to remain volatile
- Sustainability becoming a structural requirement, with stricter regulations and consumer scrutiny pushing producers toward certified, traceable and environmentally responsible supply chains

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Scale the branded and value-added portfolio to capture India's edible oil demand tailwinds, with the MD&A stating Gokul Agro is well-positioned to capture these tailwinds as it scales its branded and value-added portfolio
- Compete through an integrated model rather than scale alone, leveraging integrated sourcing, refining, port-linked infrastructure and a distribution-led model as the MD&A describes as strategically valuable given India's structural import dependence
- Build a self-reinforcing engine of adjacent businesses, with the Corporate Overview stating every investment over the past several years has been designed to reinforce the one before it and that growth beyond the commodity ceiling demands integration
- Move up the value chain into higher-margin premium, cold-pressed, fortified and speciality oil segments as health-led premiumisation reshapes product portfolios
- Extend the castor derivatives franchise into bio-based chemicals, cosmetics, lubricants and pharmaceutical excipient applications where India holds over 85% of global castor seed production

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Gokul Agro operates an integrated, port-linked manufacturing footprint across Gandhidham, Krishnapatnam, Haldia and Mangalore, and the MD&A states the Company now has 2 Million MTPA of oil refining capacity, 1 Million MTPA of seed-crushing capacity and 2.5 lacs MTPA of speciality products and biodiesel capacity. Supply-chain infrastructure supporting this platform comprises 37,000 MT of silos capacity, 2,10,000 MT of liquid storage capacity and 50,000 MT of seed and DOC warehousing capacity. During FY26 the Company invested Rs 150 cr in capital expenditure primarily for the Biodiesel plant and the Captive Solar Power project in Gujarat, reinforcing its manufacturing and operating capabilities, with net debt of Rs 297 cr described as largely reflecting investments in strategic expansion and capital expenditure. On the project side, the Directors Report records that the Company commenced operations of a biodiesel plant with a capacity of 300 MTPD during FY 2025-26, with output primarily exported to European countries where demand for renewable fuels is strong; in the prior year FY 2024-25 the Company initiated palm plantation activities in Ananthapur District, Andhra Pradesh covering 100.73 hectares of land under the National Mission on Edible Oils (NMEO), described as a significant step towards backward integration and sustainable raw material sourcing. Within existing plants, a debottlenecking step is described in the energy-conservation disclosure: an 800 TPD separator was installed in the refinery neutralisation section in place of two 400 TPD separators, increasing production capacity from 1200 TPD to 2000 TPD while reducing power consumption. Capacity utilisation is stated as averaging around 83% across refining and seed-crushing units, and captive renewable generation is in place, with power generated from wind and solar utilised in the manufacturing units and offices across all 4 locations.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Port-linked manufacturing at Gandhidham, Haldia, Krishnapatnam and Mangalore located near key ports including Kandla, strengthening sourcing efficiency, reducing transportation costs and enhancing export competitiveness
- Fully integrated value chain from seed procurement and crushing through refining, packaging and distribution, enabling flexible product mix planning and swift response to demand shifts
- Scale in refining with 2 Million MTPA capacity and capacity utilisation averaging around 83% across refining and seed-crushing units
- Distribution reach of 575+ distributors, a hub-and-spoke logistics model and presence across 28 states and 33 countries
- Institutional credibility with large food manufacturers being extended into a unified B2B and B2C trust platform, with established consumer brands Vitalife and Mahek
- Comprehensive internationally recognised food safety and quality certifications operating under a single unified quality governance framework across all products
- Over 40 years of promoter expertise in the edible oil industry, with the Chairman & Managing Director a first-generation entrepreneur with over four decades in the sector
- Unified digital core on SAP S/4HANA spanning procurement, manufacturing, inventory, finance, sales and distribution, with DCS-based real-time process monitoring and batch-level traceability
- Captive renewable power from wind and solar utilised across all four manufacturing locations, plus use of castor meal as boiler fuel in place of coal, lowering production costs
- Product-mix breadth spanning consumer edible oils, industrial castor derivatives, institutional supply, biodiesel and global exports, diversifying the demand base within the oils value chain

risks.title: Bear — key risks
risks.body:
- Single-activity concentration in edible and non-edible oils — The BRSR reports 100% of turnover from one main activity, Edible Oils, Food, FMCG and Industry Essentials, with Edible Oils & Byproducts at 90.88% and Non Edible Oils & Byproducts at 9.12% of turnover, so there is no earnings diversification outside the oils value chain.
- Commodity price volatility in an inherently thin-margin business — The Corporate Overview describes the commodity market the Company was built in as one that runs on volume, volatility and thin margins, where efficiency, integrated sourcing and logistics reach separate survival from leadership, so small swings in oilseed and edible oil prices bear directly on profitability.
- Exposure to global supply, freight and geopolitical disruption through imports and exports — The Company sells across 28 states and 33 countries with exports at 8.11% of turnover, and the forward-looking disclaimer explicitly qualifies the report by the risk factors in the MD&A, flagging that assumptions and predictions may not prove accurate.
- High workforce attrition, particularly among permanent workers — BRSR turnover rates rose year on year: permanent employees to 26.62% in FY26 from 22.32% in FY25 and permanent workers to 39.78% from 29.02%, a structural retention and operating-continuity concern in plant operations.
- Customer concentration in B2B institutional sales — The BRSR states the Company's historical strength lies in B2B sales, naming PARLE Biscuits, Haldiram Snacks, Pratap Snacks, Gopal Snacks, ITC, Britannia and Balaji Wafers among its clientele, so a small set of large food manufacturers carries meaningful volume.
- Geographic concentration of manufacturing in a small number of national plants — BRSR Section A records 4 plants and 1 office, all national with no international sites, so operational disruption at any single facility is not readily absorbed elsewhere.
- Ongoing tax and customs litigation — The notes disclose appeals pending with GST authorities, an income-tax matter under section 148 before the Gujarat High Court and a customs matter before CESTAT Ahmedabad; management assesses these as only possible and expects no material financial impact, but they remain open proceedings.
- Governance concentration in a promoter family with related-party breadth — The Board comprises 8 directors with 4 executive directors drawn from the promoter family, women are 12.50% of the Board, and the related-party roster lists numerous entities under KMP significant influence or control, raising oversight and related-party-transaction scrutiny.
